levels.name: Street, 34th St at Broadway
levels.note: The model's street level. The ground here is close to flat, unlike 42nd St.

levels.name: Main mezzanine, passages and PATH hall
levels.note: 13 ft below the street: the official rise of the escalators down to the PATH hall at 32nd St, which the long passage joins to the north mezzanine with no machine between. The north mezzanine's own depth is not listed: EL213's rise is blank. nycsubway.org's depths fit this. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: Upper ramp landing
levels.note: Design proposal: two equal 2.4 m flights aligned on one plan centreline and connected by a 2.4 m landing. Broader original stair width retained as design baseline; no slab apron beneath the sloped upper flight. Dimensions and heights assumed, not surveyed.

levels.name: N Q R W platforms
levels.note: 10 ft 1 in below the main mezzanine (EL211, official). Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: South mezzanine for the B D F M
levels.note: 25 ft below the street: the official rises of the 13 ft and 12 ft escalators down from 32nd St and 6th Ave. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: Lower bridge over the express tracks
levels.note: Design proposal: two equal 2.4 m flights aligned on one plan centreline and connected by a 2.4 m landing. Broader original stair width retained as design baseline; no slab apron beneath the sloped upper flight. Dimensions and heights assumed, not surveyed.

levels.name: B D F M platforms
levels.note: 27 ft 3 in below the main mezzanine (EL209, EL210, official). The long escalators list 28 to 30 ft. The tracks dip mid-station and the platform ceiling drops under Broadway (nycsubway.org, SubwayNut); the model draws one flat floor. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

entrances.name: Street elevator at 34th St and Broadway

known_issues.text: Rises come from the MTA's machine list. The north mezzanine's depth is not listed: it is taken from the PATH hall's, which a passage joins with no machine. The resulting depths fit nycsubway.org's 20 and 40 ft (to within 10 ft).

known_issues.topic: B D F M platforms are not flat
known_issues.text: The tracks dip mid-station and the ceiling drops under Broadway. No source gives the amounts, so one flat floor is drawn.

Settled by the Midtown South FEIS (2025): its diagram marks the stairs from control area N507 on the south B D F M mezzanine 'up to PATH concourse', and the Manhattan Mall escalators and stairs lead from that concourse up to the street. So PATH's concourse is the upper level, as drawn. The MTA's machine list names the levels the other way round. Where EL200X lands is still not listed.
Elevators list 27 ft 3 in and the long escalators 28 to 30 ft for the same two levels. Both are official; the difference may be that dip.

The Midtown South FEIS gives three stairs a side to this mezzanine (uptown P2, P4, P11; downtown P1, P3, P12). OSM maps three and two and a walking description says the opposite; the third downtown stair (P3) is added where the diagram orders it, its exact place assumed.
ES221 to ES224 share one position, and the long escalators and platform elevators cluster near mid-station. EL209 and EL210 are placed by a walking description instead.
One entrance named 34 St-Herald Sq is filed under complex 602, which is 14 St-Union Sq. Taken as a mistake.
None was found. Halls are inside the MTA's outlines and reach every stair and machine, but their shapes are not surveyed. Candy Chan's axonometric was used to check how spaces join.

Only public circulation is modelled. Staff rooms, plant rooms and emergency exits are left out on purpose. PATH's platforms are not modelled, nor the closed Gimbels passage. Street easements at 32nd St without their own machines are not drawn.

Control area A022A (shown near ES229 and ES230 with high entry/exit turnstiles, no count given) and stair ML5 (13.67 ft, uptown platform to the bridge level near P6 and P8) are in the FEIS diagram but not modelled: their places and runs are unclear from a diagram that is not to scale. The FEIS text also disagrees with itself on one corner (IND S8/M8) and names the 34th St and 6th Ave stairs differently from its diagram.

Stairs with a NYCT element number carry its width from the Midtown South FEIS (feet, converted). The short stair from the landing and the bridge stair it faces are drawn 2.4 m, narrower than listed (8.25 and 9.67 ft), so that one lines up with the other.

Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.
